analysis:
All four units are documentation-only: a test.md excerpt, provider-release.md metadata, its patch and its base text. No executable code, workflow, script or coordinator source is supplied, so the claims below are unverified.

The patch documents a new `cluster_runtime` block in the signed-release `POST /v1/releases` payload (provider-release.md head ~604-612 and the new 'Cluster Runtime Facts' section at 651-792). A coordinator that accepts it derives per-build cluster approvals, pair-serving grants and public parity qualifications automatically. Those were previously operator-posted. This moves authority toward A-005 (release API key), A-016/A-017 (serving authorization and build qualifications) and T-054, and it relies on the following:
(1) Facts come from the final app's own CLI (`runtime-facts`, `--describe-runtime`) run with `env -i` after the signing keychain is deleted. The doc says the step fails unless the keychain is gone, and that it removes secret-derived values from GITHUB_ENV. Those are CI controls described in prose and not visible here.
(2) Model metadata is fetched from the public catalog and model CDN (`manifest.json`, `config.json`, `catalog.json`). The doc says integrity failures fail the step. The mechanism is not visible. A compromised catalog or CDN could shape declared models and modalities.
(3) The block is gated by per-environment `*_CLUSTER_RUNTIME_ENABLED` variables. `validate` and `prepare` enforce canonical form, ID length of at most 128 bytes and a 64 KiB body limit, and the coordinator reads the block strictly (DisallowUnknownFields). The enforcement is in unseen scripts and platform code.
(4) Catalog capacity bounds (64 approvals, 64 grants, 256 qualifications) mean older releases' entries are dropped, and operator entries are never displaced. That is an availability and eviction consideration, not a regression.
The docs state that rollout order must have the platform accept the block before it is enabled. The pinned platform handler link is df61dd6f, which I could not verify.

The qualify-sdk to qualify-sdk-shard renaming and the five-shard audit claim affect the release gate. The doc says signing requires `qualify-sdk`, which passes only if all shards run the full suite, but the workflow implementation is unseen.

No concrete security regression is evidenced in the supplied text. The threat model likely needs updating for release-derived cluster approvals and public qualification. A deeper review of the workflows, `scripts/provider-cluster-runtime-models.py`, `provider-cluster-runtime-facts.sh`, `provider-release-publication.py` and the platform handler is recommended.
